turns.query: Why did PAT decrease in FY26 compared to FY25 and what happened to SAED windfall tax?
turns.spoken_summary: ₹32,894 crore across 1 years (FY26). Highest: FY26 (₹32,894 crore). Note 28: Complete History of SAED Windfall Tax, OIDB Cess & Royalty on ONGC (FY17–FY26) (Note 28 (Statutory Levies — SAED Windfall Tax)): Under Schedule III Note 28 (Statutory Levies), ONGC pays three major production levies to the Government: (1) Royalty (10% on offshore crude/gas, 12.5% on onshore crude, 10% on onshore gas), (2) OIDB Cess (20% ad-valorem on crude oil since union budget revision), and (3) Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED / Windfall Tax) introduced by the Government of India on 1 July 2022. When Brent surged to $96.13/bbl in FY23 during the Russia-Ukraine conflict, SAED extracted ₹10,964 Cr from ONGC, pushing total Statutory Levies to a record ₹45,284.2 Cr (29.1% of Gross Revenue) and capping net crude realisation at $75.30/bbl. In FY24, fortnightly SAED revisions reduced SAED to ₹6,433.5 Cr (total levies ₹36,797.5 Cr). In December 2024 (FY25), the Government of India formally abolished SAED on domestic crude production; FY25 SAED fell to ₹3,769.8 Cr (total levies ₹30,968 Cr). In FY26, ONGC enjoyed its first full year of zero SAED windfall tax (₹0 Cr), bringing total Statutory Levies down to ₹25,999 Cr (Royalty ₹12,965 Cr + OIDB Cess ₹13,034 Cr) and saving ₹3,770 Cr YoY. Details are on screen.

turns.query: What action should the Finance Director take to improve upstream margins in FY27?
turns.spoken_summary: ₹32,894 crore across 1 years (FY26). Highest: FY26 (₹32,894 crore). Director (Finance) 5-Point Action Playbook for ONGC Margin, Capex & Subsidiary Optimization (FY26–FY27) (Director (Finance) & CMD Strategic Action Playbook): Five concrete, quantified Director (Finance) interventions based on FY17–FY26 audited statements: (1) Gas Realization Uplift (Note 24): Reallocate ₹4,200 Cr infill & workover capex to 48 New Well Gas (NWNG) wells in Bassein, Daman, and Tripura eligible for the 20% price premium ($7.80/MMBtu vs $6.50/MMBtu APM ceiling), adding +₹1,480 Cr/yr in high-margin revenue; (2) Mature Field Lifting Cost Turnaround (Note 26): Ring-fence 12 high-water-cut (>78%) marginal clusters in Mehsana, Ankleshwar, and Cambay into revenue-sharing Production Enhancement Contracts (PEC) (-₹620 Cr/yr direct opex) and deploy 180 MW captive solar power via ONGC Green Ltd for ESP/SRP artificial lift (-₹310 Cr/yr power expense); (3) Deepwater Dry-Well Risk Governance (Note 32): Mandate 30%-40% PI international technical partner carry before drilling Category-II/III ultra-deepwater wildcat wells (>₹750 Cr/well) in Andaman and KG-UDW, protecting ₹1,500–₹2,000 Cr/yr in P&L write-offs; (4) OPaL Post-Recapitalization Breakeven (Note 10): Following the ₹18,365 Cr CCD-to-equity conversion (95.69% stake), substitute imported naphtha at OPaL with 100% captive C2-C3 from Dahej/Hazira and complete SEZ exit to save ₹1,150 Cr/yr and reach PAT breakeven by Q3 FY27; (5) Treasury & Debt Optimization (Notes 15, 21): Use unrestricted treasury cash (out of ₹33,500 Cr Cash & Bank) to retire ₹1,730 Cr short-term working capital debt, saving ₹135+ Cr/yr in Note 34 Finance Costs. turns.query: Why did PAT crash in FY20 and why did PAT triple in FY22?
turns.spoken_summary: ₹65,016 crore across 3 years (FY20–FY22). Highest: FY22 (₹40,306 crore) and FY20 (₹13,464 crore). Notes 36 & 37: Why FY20 PAT Crashed (₹13,464 Cr) and Why FY22 PAT Tripled to ₹40,306 Cr (Note 36 (Exceptional Items) & Note 37 (Section 115BAA Tax)): In Q4 FY20, the COVID-19 pandemic caused global crude benchmarks to crash below $25/bbl, triggering a non-cash Exceptional Impairment charge of -₹4,899 Cr (Note 36) across mature cash-generating units and cutting FY20 Standalone PAT by 49.7% to ₹13,464 Cr. In FY21, crude oil realisation averaged an 18-year low of $42.78/bbl and gas APM prices dropped to $1.96/MMBtu, depressing Gross Revenue to ₹68,141 Cr; a partial impairment reversal of +₹1,375 Cr supported FY21 PAT at ₹11,246 Cr (PBT ₹16,403 Cr). In FY22, two historic events drove Standalone PAT up 258% to ₹40,306 Cr on PBT of ₹41,040 Cr: (1) Crude oil realisation rebounded 80% to $76.96/bbl, prompting an Exceptional Impairment Reversal of +₹7,178 Cr (Note 36); and (2) ONGC elected to migrate to the new corporate tax regime under Section 115BAA of the Income Tax Act (25.168% statutory tax rate vs 34.944% earlier), resulting in a one-time Deferred Tax liability reversal of -₹8,846 Cr (Note 37) against Current Tax of ₹9,580 Cr, reducing net Tax Expense for FY22 to just ₹734 Cr (1.79% effective tax rate). Details are on screen.

In FY21, crude oil realisation averaged an 18-year low of $42.78/bbl and gas APM prices dropped to $1.96/MMBtu, depressing Gross Revenue to ₹68,141 Cr; a partial impairment reversal of +₹1,375 Cr supported FY21 PAT at ₹11,246 Cr (PBT ₹16,403 Cr). In FY22, two historic events drove Standalone PAT up 258% to ₹40,306 Cr on PBT of ₹41,040 Cr: (1) Crude oil realisation rebounded 80% to $76.96/bbl, prompting an Exceptional Impairment Reversal of +₹7,178 Cr (Note 36); and (2) ONGC elected to migrate to the new corporate tax regime under Section 115BAA of the Income Tax Act (25.168% statutory tax rate vs 34.944% earlier), resulting in a one-time Deferred Tax liability reversal of -₹8,846 Cr (Note 37) against Current Tax of ₹9,580 Cr, reducing net Tax Expense for FY22 to just ₹734 Cr (1.79% effective tax rate).
FY22 accounts for 62.0% of the total (₹40,306 cr of ₹65,016 cr).

Note 28: Complete History of SAED Windfall Tax, OIDB Cess & Royalty on ONGC (FY17–FY26) (Note 28 (Statutory Levies — SAED Windfall Tax)): Under Schedule III Note 28 (Statutory Levies), ONGC pays three major production levies to the Government: (1) Royalty (10% on offshore crude/gas, 12.5% on onshore crude, 10% on onshore gas), (2) OIDB Cess (20% ad-valorem on crude oil since union budget revision), and (3) Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED / Windfall Tax) introduced by the Government of India on 1 July 2022. When Brent surged to $96.13/bbl in FY23 during the Russia-Ukraine conflict, SAED extracted ₹10,964 Cr from ONGC, pushing total Statutory Levies to a record ₹45,284.2 Cr (29.1% of Gross Revenue) and capping net crude realisation at $75.30/bbl. In FY24, fortnightly SAED revisions reduced SAED to ₹6,433.5 Cr (total levies ₹36,797.5 Cr). In December 2024 (FY25), the Government of India formally abolished SAED on domestic crude production; FY25 SAED fell to ₹3,769.8 Cr (total levies ₹30,968 Cr). In FY26, ONGC enjoyed its first full year of zero SAED windfall tax (₹0 Cr), bringing total Statutory Levies down to ₹25,999 Cr (Royalty ₹12,965 Cr + OIDB Cess ₹13,034 Cr) and saving ₹3,770 Cr YoY. Details are on screen.

turns.query: Why did exploration dry-well write-offs and DD&A increase in FY25 and FY26?
turns.spoken_summary: ₹13,520 crore across 2 years (FY25–FY26). Highest: FY25 (₹7,680 crore) and FY26 (₹5,840 crore). Notes 32 & 33: Exploration Dry-Well Write-Offs & KG-DWN-98/2 Depletion Impact (FY23–FY26) (Note 32 (Exploration Costs Written Off) & Note 33 (DD&A)): Under Successful Efforts Method (Ind-AS 106 / Schedule III Note 32), geological & geophysical (G&G) survey expenditure is expensed as incurred, and exploratory wells that do not establish commercial reserves are charged off as Dry Wells Written Off. In FY23, deepwater exploratory well write-offs in KG and Andaman basins spiked Exploration Costs Written Off to ₹10,031.2 Cr (Survey ₹1,980.2 Cr + Dry Wells ₹8,051 Cr). In FY24, higher exploratory success lowered write-offs to ₹5,568.5 Cr, helping Standalone PAT reach a record ₹40,526 Cr. In FY25, accelerated frontier basin appraisal caused Exploration Costs Written Off to jump by ₹4,257.3 Cr (+76.5%) to ₹9,825.8 Cr (Survey ₹2,145.8 Cr + Dry Wells ₹7,680 Cr), while commissioning of KG-DWN-98/2 Cluster-II deepwater facilities increased DD&A (Note 33) from ₹20,495.5 Cr in FY24 to ₹22,924.2 Cr in FY25 and ₹25,197.0 Cr in FY26. In FY26, Exploration Costs Written Off moderated to ₹7,790 Cr (Survey ₹1,950 Cr + Dry Wells ₹5,840 Cr). Director (Finance) Action: Mandate 30%-40% PI farm-out risk-sharing on frontier ultra-deepwater wildcat wells (>₹750 Cr/well) to cap single-well dry-hole P&L exposure at ≤₹450 Cr. Details are on screen.

turns.query: Why did borrowings jump from zero in FY17 to ₹25,592 crore in FY18?
turns.spoken_summary: ₹25,592 crore across 2 years (FY17–FY18). Highest: FY18 (₹25,592 crore) and FY17 (₹0 crore). turns.query: Why did CWIP decline in FY25 and FY26 as KG-DWN-98/2 Cluster-II was commissioned?
turns.spoken_summary: ₹75,370 crore across 2 years (FY25–FY26). Highest: FY25 (₹38,450 crore) and FY26 (₹36,920 crore). Notes 32 & 33: Exploration Dry-Well Write-Offs & KG-DWN-98/2 Depletion Impact (FY23–FY26) (Note 32 (Exploration Costs Written Off) & Note 33 (DD&A)): Under Successful Efforts Method (Ind-AS 106 / Schedule III Note 32), geological & geophysical (G&G) survey expenditure is expensed as incurred, and exploratory wells that do not establish commercial reserves are charged off as Dry Wells Written Off. In FY23, deepwater exploratory well write-offs in KG and Andaman basins spiked Exploration Costs Written Off to ₹10,031.2 Cr (Survey ₹1,980.2 Cr + Dry Wells ₹8,051 Cr). In FY24, higher exploratory success lowered write-offs to ₹5,568.5 Cr, helping Standalone PAT reach a record ₹40,526 Cr. In FY25, accelerated frontier basin appraisal caused Exploration Costs Written Off to jump by ₹4,257.3 Cr (+76.5%) to ₹9,825.8 Cr (Survey ₹2,145.8 Cr + Dry Wells ₹7,680 Cr), while commissioning of KG-DWN-98/2 Cluster-II deepwater facilities increased DD&A (Note 33) from ₹20,495.5 Cr in FY24 to ₹22,924.2 Cr in FY25 and ₹25,197.0 Cr in FY26. In FY26, Exploration Costs Written Off moderated to ₹7,790 Cr (Survey ₹1,950 Cr + Dry Wells ₹5,840 Cr). Director (Finance) Action: Mandate 30%-40% PI farm-out risk-sharing on frontier ultra-deepwater wildcat wells (>₹750 Cr/well) to cap single-well dry-hole P&L exposure at ≤₹450 Cr. Details are on screen.

turns.sql:
WITH capex AS (
  SELECT asset_wc_id, SUM(actual_spend_inr_cr) AS capex_cr
  FROM `ongc-hr-finance-agent.hrfin_silver.capex_budget`
  WHERE fiscal_year BETWEEN 'FY22' AND 'FY26'
  GROUP BY asset_wc_id),
res AS (
  SELECT asset_wc_id, SUM(reserves_2p_total_mmtoe) AS reserves_2p_mmtoe
  FROM `ongc-hr-finance-agent.hrfin_silver.reserves_annual`
  WHERE fiscal_year = 'FY26'
  GROUP BY asset_wc_id),
j AS (SELECT c.asset_wc_id, c.capex_cr, r.reserves_2p_mmtoe FROM capex c LEFT JOIN res r USING (asset_wc_id)),
a AS (SELECT SUM(capex_cr) / NULLIF(SUM(reserves_2p_mmtoe), 0) AS avg_cr_per_mmtoe FROM j WHERE reserves_2p_mmtoe > 0)
SELECT j.asset_wc_id AS asset,
  ROUND(j.capex_cr, 0) AS capex_cr,
  ROUND(j.capex_cr * 100.0 / SUM(j.capex_cr) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_capex,
  ROUND(j.reserves_2p_mmtoe, 1) AS reserves_2p_mmtoe,
  ROUND(j.capex_cr / NULLIF(j.reserves_2p_mmtoe, 0), 1) AS capex_cr_per_mmtoe,
  ROUND(a.avg_cr_per_mmtoe, 1) AS avg_capex_cr_per_mmtoe,
  (j.reserves_2p_mmtoe > 0 AND j.capex_cr / j.reserves_2p_mmtoe < 0.5 * a.avg_cr_per_mmtoe) AS under_invested
FROM j CROSS JOIN a
ORDER BY j.capex_cr DESC

turns.spoken_summary: ₹349,979.5 crore across 10 years (fy = FY26, FY17–FY26). Highest: FY24 (₹57,101 crore) and FY26 (₹49,793 crore). Marriage of ONGC Standalone Annual Report & Yahoo Finance (ONGC.NS) Consolidated Financials (Consolidated Schedule III & Yahoo Finance (ONGC.NS)): Yahoo Finance (`ONGC.NS/financials`) defaults to Consolidated Ind-AS Financials for the ONGC Group, which consolidates ONGC Standalone with Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL, 54.90% stake acquired Jan 2018), Mangalore Refinery & Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL, 71.63%), ONGC Videsh Ltd (OVL, 100%), ONGC Petro additions Ltd (OPaL, 95.69%), and ONGC Tripura Power Co Ltd (OTPC, 50%). Because HPCL and MRPL are downstream oil marketing & refining companies, Consolidated Revenue (`₹6,48,920 Cr` in FY26; `₹6,63,262 Cr` in FY25) is ~4.8x Standalone E&P Revenue (`₹1,32,508 Cr` in FY26; `₹1,37,846 Cr` in FY25). In FY23, Consolidated PAT (`₹35,440 Cr`) was lower than Standalone PAT (`₹38,829 Cr`) because HPCL suffered ₹6,980 Cr of retail fuel marketing under-recoveries during the global oil spike. In FY24 (`₹57,101 Cr` Consolidated PAT vs `₹40,526 Cr` Standalone PAT) and FY26 (`₹49,793 Cr` Consolidated PAT vs `₹32,894 Cr` Standalone PAT), strong refining GRMs at HPCL/MRPL and OVL international recovery drove Consolidated PAT significantly above Standalone PAT. turns.query: Why was Consolidated PAT lower than Standalone PAT in FY23 but higher in FY24 and FY26?
turns.spoken_summary: Consolidated group PAT ONGC.NS (₹ cr) — FY24: ₹57,101 crore vs FY25: ₹38,329 crore vs FY26: ₹49,793 crore (fy in FY26, FY23, FY24, FY24–FY26). Notes 32 & 33: Exploration Dry-Well Write-Offs & KG-DWN-98/2 Depletion Impact (FY23–FY26) (Note 32 (Exploration Costs Written Off) & Note 33 (DD&A)): Under Successful Efforts Method (Ind-AS 106 / Schedule III Note 32), geological & geophysical (G&G) survey expenditure is expensed as incurred, and exploratory wells that do not establish commercial reserves are charged off as Dry Wells Written Off. In FY23, deepwater exploratory well write-offs in KG and Andaman basins spiked Exploration Costs Written Off to ₹10,031.2 Cr (Survey ₹1,980.2 Cr + Dry Wells ₹8,051 Cr). In FY24, higher exploratory success lowered write-offs to ₹5,568.5 Cr, helping Standalone PAT reach a record ₹40,526 Cr. In FY25, accelerated frontier basin appraisal caused Exploration Costs Written Off to jump by ₹4,257.3 Cr (+76.5%) to ₹9,825.8 Cr (Survey ₹2,145.8 Cr + Dry Wells ₹7,680 Cr), while commissioning of KG-DWN-98/2 Cluster-II deepwater facilities increased DD&A (Note 33) from ₹20,495.5 Cr in FY24 to ₹22,924.2 Cr in FY25 and ₹25,197.0 Cr in FY26. In FY26, Exploration Costs Written Off moderated to ₹7,790 Cr (Survey ₹1,950 Cr + Dry Wells ₹5,840 Cr). Director (Finance) Action: Mandate 30%-40% PI farm-out risk-sharing on frontier ultra-deepwater wildcat wells (>₹750 Cr/well) to cap single-well dry-hole P&L exposure at ≤₹450 Cr. -- Answer Key SQL: X4
-- Question: What is our pension and post-retirement medical liability, and its 5-year trend?

SELECT
    fiscal_year,
    SUM(IF(LOWER(scheme_type) = 'prbs pension', actuarial_liability_inr_cr, 0)) AS prbs_pension_liability_cr,

ORDER BY fiscal_year;

turns.sql:
-- Answer Key SQL: X6
-- Question: How much capex went to ONGC Green / renewables vs. the Net Zero 2038 path, and how many people have been reskilled?
-- Type: data
-- Semantic audit 2026-10-20: Answers all three parts: green capex per FY (FY22-FY26) with running cumulative (sum of annual_capex -
-- the stored cumulative_capex column does not reconcile), share of company capex, MW installed, roadmap milestone
-- flag, and distinct employees completing renewable reskilling (counted once, at first completion). Old SQL showed FY26 by technology only, no reskilling.
-- GAP: no Net Zero 2038 spend trajectory exists in the data; only a boolean milestone flag.
WITH g AS (
    SELECT fiscal_year,
        SUM(annual_capex_inr_cr) AS green_capex_cr,
        SUM(installed_capacity_mw) AS installed_mw,
        LOGICAL_AND(net_zero_2038_roadmap_milestone_met) AS all_roadmap_milestones_met
    FROM energy_transition
    GROUP BY fiscal_year
),
first_completion AS (
    SELECT emp_id, MIN(fiscal_year) AS first_fy
    FROM training_records
    WHERE is_renewable_reskilling AND LOWER(completion_status) = 'completed'
    GROUP BY emp_id
),
r AS (
    SELECT first_fy AS fiscal_year, COUNT(*) AS employees_newly_reskilled
    FROM first_completion
    GROUP BY first_fy
)
SELECT
    g.fiscal_year,
    ROUND(g.green_capex_cr, 1) AS green_capex_cr,
    ROUND(SUM(g.green_capex_cr) OVER (ORDER BY g.fiscal_year), 1) AS cumulative_green_capex_cr,
    c.total_capex_spent_inr_cr AS company_capex_cr,
    ROUND(g.green_capex_cr * 100 / c.total_capex_spent_inr_cr, 1) AS green_share_of_capex_pct,
    g.installed_mw,
    g.all_roadmap_milestones_met,
    r.employees_newly_reskilled,
    SUM(r.employees_newly_reskilled) OVER (ORDER BY g.fiscal_year) AS cumulative_distinct_employees_reskilled
FROM g
JOIN corporate_financials c ON c.fiscal_year = g.fiscal_year
LEFT JOIN r ON r.fiscal_year = g.fiscal_year
ORDER BY g.fiscal_year;

-- Question: What is capex utilisation (budget vs. revised estimate vs. actual) by asset for the current year?

SELECT

    ROUND(SUM(cb.budget_estimate_be_inr_cr), 1) AS be_ytd_cr,
    ROUND(SUM(cb.revised_estimate_re_inr_cr), 1) AS re_ytd_cr,
    ROUND(SUM(cb.actual_spend_inr_cr), 1) AS actual_ytd_cr,
    ROUND(SUM(cb.actual_spend_inr_cr) * 100 / NULLIF(SUM(cb.budget_estimate_be_inr_cr), 0), 1) AS utilisation_vs_be_pct,
    ROUND(SUM(cb.actual_spend_inr_cr) * 100 / NULLIF(SUM(cb.revised_estimate_re_inr_cr), 0), 1) AS utilisation_vs_re_pct,
